features: NO DATABASE CHANGES — One topic: the sale or donation of bare ownership with reserved usufruct, the case of parents who donate the home to their children and go on living there. And a few changes of behaviour that apply outside reserved usufruct too, listed first.

ALSO CHANGES OUTSIDE RESERVED USUFRUCT: THE TICK — The «What will change» panel does not ask for the tick when no share changes hands. Shares that stay with whoever holds them — by law (the usufructuary's ordinary expenses, the bare owner's extraordinary ones), because they are made only of prior balances, or because the expense belongs entirely to the seller — appear in the «Shares this transfer does not touch» box, with no tick. This also applies to the creation and termination of a usufruct, the sale of bare ownership alone and the sale of full ownership.

ALSO CHANGES OUTSIDE RESERVED USUFRUCT: THE TEXTS ON WHO REMAINS LIABLE — The sentence for the creation of a usufruct said that towards the condominium liability follows «the nature of the expense»: since 2013 bare owner and usufructuary are jointly liable (art. 67 ult. co. disp. att. c.c.), and the nature of the expense matters between them; this also changes in the history of creations already recorded. The joint-liability note, in the sale of bare ownership alone, also mentions the usufructuary and art. 67, by name only when the program knows for certain which share the usufruct is on; a sale dated in the previous year gets the note even if only the current financial year is recorded; «no share is in the buyer's name» states the exception of balances in the unit's name, which are charged when the plan is generated.

ALSO CHANGES OUTSIDE RESERVED USUFRUCT: HISTORY AND CANCELLATION — From «Edit association» the role of a row touched by a transfer can no longer be changed, even when closed and even for transfers recorded with the previous version; share, dates and notes can, and to correct the role you cancel the transfer. Cancellation no longer gives a needless warning for a previous-year final accounts plan generated afterwards. In the history, rows carry the transfer's name with a capital letter, and usufruct reads «Usufruct · creation» or «Usufruct · termination». The example in the gate note said «settlement agreed between the parties», and whoever followed it wrote the waiver in the note without ticking it: now it is neutral.

THE CHECKBOX — In the sale form, «Whoever sells or donates remains usufructuary». The seller stays on the same share as usufructuary, the buyer enters as bare owner; the share is the seller's whole share, and the reservation can only be declared by a full owner. In the history the transfer is called «Sale or donation with reserved usufruct», and it is cancelled like any other. Usufruct to a person other than the seller is still refused: it is recorded by hand, and the message now says that rows opened by hand count for the allocation as open since forever.

WHO PAYS WHAT — In instalments already issued and in the drafts of plans already issued, ordinary expenses stay with the seller, who is the usufructuary (art. 1004 c.c.): they are not settled. Extraordinary expenses follow the accrual — the resolution date, or the one declared on the invoice — and from the day of the deed belong to the bare owner (art. 1005 c.c.). A plan generated or recalculated after the deed charges according to the table's coefficients: items on «Owner» go to the buyer of the bare ownership. For ordinary expenses to stay with the seller, the item goes on «Usufructuary», not on «Tenant», which on a leased unit would make the tenant pay them. The panel says so when it reads it in the allocation of a plan not yet issued.

WHO REMAINS LIABLE — From the day of the deed, bare owner and usufructuary are jointly liable towards the condominium (art. 67 ult. co.). Whether the buyer of the bare ownership is also liable for the seller's arrears (art. 63 co. 4) case law has not made clear: the program says so, and the administrator decides. The certified copy is recorded as in any sale, but it does not release the seller, who remains usufructuary. The joint-liability note keeps the arrears and the shares after the deed separate.
THE TWO PARENTS — The second reservation on the same unit — the other parent donating their own half — adds to the first, as in an ordinary sale. Once both are recorded, the unit is consistent again.

THE LIMITS — A unit partly in full ownership and partly in bare ownership and usufruct (the reservation of only one co-owner, with the other remaining full owner): plans generated or recalculated cannot split it, and the panel warns about it with names and shares. In units under usufruct, ordinary expenses on «Owner» items go to the bare owner in plans, while the settlement on issued instalments gives them to the usufructuary: this will be brought to a single rule, after hearing from administrators. A balance in the unit's name, in a plan generated after a transfer, goes to whoever is the holder when the plan is generated. Selling part of one's own share is not provided for, and «The share changes» currently lets it be recorded the wrong way. All four will be decided before the 1.11 stable release. When one of the two usufructuary parents dies, who receives their share of the usufruct arrives with succession.

FOR DEVELOPERS — A new, permanent test file, InvariantiPassaggiTest, checks across all combinations of transfers the rules that must never break: a transfer does not change the unit's total, the settlement pairs sum to zero, the preview is what gets written, cancellation puts everything back as it was. A new transfer type is added to the list of scenarios with a few lines.
